c.tagline: Gleaming white marble monuments amid the Karakum Desert.

taxi.color: mostly white or unmarked private cars
taxi.fareNote: Meters are rare; agree on the fare, ideally in writing, before the ride, especially from the airport.

emergency.note: Fire is 01. English-speaking response capacity is limited; hotel staff or a tour guide are often the fastest route to help.

avoid.reason: Heavily controlled — avoid photographing government/military buildings; carry ID at all times

hood_desc: Ashgabat's marble-clad hotel and government strip along Archabil Highway, packed with fountains, parks and modern towers; suits travelers who want polish and comfort but don't mind taxiing everywhere.

The ceremonial heart of the city near the Presidential Palace and ministries, dominated by monuments and wide empty boulevards; best for business and official visitors prioritizing proximity to government sites.
The most walkable, lived-in part of town around Turkmenbashy Avenue and the Gulistan (Russian) Bazaar, near the train station; suits budget travelers wanting easier access to everyday local life.
A quieter southern district built around the 2017 Asian Games venues; a calm, less showy base good for those attending events or wanting distance from the marble showpiece core.
The city's edge where Archabil Highway climbs toward the Köpetdag mountains and the cableway station; suits travelers wanting mountain views and hiking access over central convenience.

water.note: Avoid tap water; use bottled or filtered water.

transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash in manat directly to the driver or conductor; there is no rechargeable transit card for visitors. Fares are just a few cents, but exact change is appreciated. Shared minivan (marshrutka) routes are also common.
transit.hours: Buses and trolleybuses run roughly 6:00-23:00; there is no dedicated night bus network, so taxis are the only late-night option.
transit.note: Routes aren't published in English and drivers navigate by landmark rather than street name; having your destination written in Russian or Turkmen helps a lot.

train: Ashgabat Railway Station (domestic trains to Turkmenabat, Mary, Dashoguz and Turkmenbashy)
bus: Intercity buses and marshrutkas from Ashgabat's main bus station to regional cities

transit.m: Public city bus into center (~30-40 min)

tip.r: Not a deeply rooted custom; rounding up or leaving roughly 5-10% at restaurants used by tourists is appreciated but not expected elsewhere.
